title: SLO contract table pilot and negotiation canvas (45d)
content:
Purpose:
Run a focused 45-day pilot to operationalize SLO negotiation as a lightweight contract-table process between SRE, Product, and Platform. Goal is to make SLOs actionable, testable in canaries, and to produce a repeatable negotiation canvas that Product teams can use to set realistic availability/latency contracts for model-serving endpoints.

Why this is different / problem statement:
- Lots of SLO docs exist but teams struggle at the negotiation step: tradeoffs between p99 latency, cost, and feature risk are unclear.
- We need a compact, standardized artifact (the contract table) that reduces back-and-forth and provides a clear canary rollout plan and rollback triggers.
- Focus on first-party model-serving flows (hosted API + dedicated) where multi-tenant capacity and latency budgets are most fragile.

Success criteria (pilot-level):
- 3 product teams onboarded to the contract-table negotiation workflow.
- Canary rollout executed for 2 endpoints with measurable telemetry (p95, p99, error-budget burn, cold-starts).
- Playbook and template created and accepted by Product/Ops.
- One post-mortem with action items and adopted checklist items in the SLO playbook.

Core artifacts to deliver:
- Contract table template: service, route, customer-tier, SLO target, measurement window, error budget policy, rollback triggers, fallback model variant, cost guardrails.
- Negotiation canvas: one-page checklist for cross-functional workshop.
- Canary runbook: step-by-step rollout, gating checks, dashboards, alert rules.
- Decision log and lightweight runbook for emergency downgrade paths.

45-day timeline (high level):
- Days 1–8 (Prep): inventory candidate endpoints, draft contract-table templates, instrument missing metrics, create canary clusters.
  - Tasks: identify owners, map existing dashboards, create JIRA epic SRE-2027.
- Days 9–18 (Negotiation workshops): run 60–90 minute workshops with each product team using the negotiation canvas. Capture agreed contract-table entries.
  - Deliverable: signed draft contract table per endpoint (Slack ack + doc).
- Days 19–32 (Canary + monitor): perform staggered canaries per contract (10% traffic -> 30% -> 60%), run daily checks, escalate when gates fail.
  - Metrics to watch: error budget consumption, p95/p99 latency, user-visible error rate, cold-start ratio, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.
- Days 33–40 (Evaluation & adjustments): synthesize telemetry, run targeted load tests to exercise limits, update contract table parameters.
- Days 41–45 (Finalize & handoff): publish canonical templates, bake into SRE onboarding, run retrospective, create follow-up backlog.

Roles & responsibilities (suggested):
- SRE Lead (Maya P.): program owner, guarantees instrumentation and runbook correctness.
- Product Owner (Team rep): defines customer-level availability/latency priorities and accepts tradeoffs.
- Platform Eng: prepares canary infra, traffic shaping, and autoscaling knobs.
- Observability Eng: dashboards, alerting, and synthetic checks.
- Solutions Eng / SE: customer impact liaison for enterprise tenants.

Negotiation canvas (one-page checklist):
- Business goal: primary KPI the SLO protects (e.g., feature conversion, page load).
- Endpoint & route definition: exact API + variants.
- Customer tiers impacted: free / paid / enterprise.
- Proposed SLOs: availability (>=99.9 over 30d), p95 latency (<=250ms), p99 latency (<=600ms) -- example placeholders.
- Measurement window & burn policy: 30d window, 14-day smoothing, immediate alert at 10% burn in 24h.
- Fallback plan: model variant / cached path / synthetic reply.
- Cost constraints: expected per-token cost caps, acceptable autoscale headroom.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p99 > threshold for 30m OR error-budget burn rate above X.
- Acceptance: sign-off owners + communication list.

Concrete canary runbook (short):
- Pre-checks: dashboards populated, synthetic traffic test passing, rollback scripts validated.
- Phase 1: 10% traffic for 6 hours. Checkpoints at 30m, 3h, 6h.
- Phase 2: 30% traffic for 12 hours. Checkpoints every 2h.
- Phase 3: 60–100% for 24h. Final sign-off by Product and SRE.
- Emergency rollback: trigger if p99 breach sustained for 30 minutes AND error budget burn accelerates.

Instrumentation & dashboards (work items):
- Add route-level p99/p95 histograms to central metrics.
- Synthesize error budget burn dashboards per tenant tier.
- Add budgeted-cost dashboard (tokens / GPU-minutes) to show cost vs SLO.
- Create synthetic probes to exercise cold-start paths.

Decision log & communication plan:
- Every negotiation workshop gets one entry in decision log (Confluence) summarizing agreed SLOs, owners, and rollback policy.
- Slack channel for pilot: #slo-contract-table-pilot (temporary); create announcement cadence: weekly status + immediate alerts on canary gating failures.

Risk register (top items):
- Measurement gaps: service lacks per-route p99 metric => high risk. Mitigation: short EPIC to add headers/labels.
- Cost shock: SLO tightening drives autoscale. Mitigation: cost guardrail in contract table and pre-approved budget.
- Tenant impact: canary routing mistakes could hit prod tenants. Mitigation: traffic-shaping validation and only internal tenants for early phases.

Open questions (to resolve in first workshop):
- What is the canonical window for p99 SLOs across model-serving? 30d or 14d?
- What threshold of error budget burn should autoscale allow before enforcement?
- How to represent multi-model fallbacks in the contract table when model quality differs?

Immediate TODOs (next 7 days):
- [ ] Create Confluence decision-log page and link in linked_artifacts (Evan).
- [ ] Wire up p99 histograms for candidate endpoint /api/generate (Observability).
- [ ] Schedule 3 negotiation workshops (Leah).
- [ ] Provision canary pool and traffic control (Platform Eng).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "soft SLO" class for developer-friendly experimental routes where enforcement should be lax and telemetry prioritized over rollback.
- Potential template field: "grace period" (minutes) to allow transient GC/compaction hits without triggering rollback.
- Could prototype a small UI in the Console that surfaces the contract table with one-click rollback and annotated metrics.

Post-pilot artifacts expected:
- SLO contract-table template (final).
- Canary runbook in repo: /runbooks/slo-contract-canary.md.
- Playbook update: SRE onboarding + Product playbooks.
- Rollout plan to scale the workflow to ~10 services in Q2.

Retrospective questions we will ask at day 45:
- Did the contract-table reduce negotiation time? (measure workshop length + follow-up tickets).
- Were rollback triggers useful or noisy?
- Did teams feel empowered to trade latency vs cost?
- What automation gaps remain to make this repeatable?

Contact / owners: Maya Patel (SRE lead) maya@redwood.ai, Evan Zhao (Observability) evan@redwood.ai
